THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The landloosers have filed these appeals seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge, Vijaypur (henceforth referred to as 'reference Court') in LAC Nos.86/2012, 82/2012 and 80/2012 vide its judgment and award dated 04.03.2015.
2.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge, Vijaypur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The following are the details of the lands belonging to the appellants/landloosers:-
 Sl. MFA Nos. Survey Extent Village  No. Number  1 201977/2017 59/1B 1 acre Hegadihal  25 guntas  2 201976/2017 58/2B/1 2 acres Hegadihal  4 guntas  3 201978/2017 59/2B/2 2 acres Hegadihal  1 gunta 3.

The aforesaid lands were acquired for construction of Minor Irrigation Tank in terms of the notification issued NC: 2023:KHC-K:5597 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (henceforth referred to as 'Act') bearing No.LAQ-SR-13/2009- 10 dated 06.05.2010.
4.
A common award dated 16.10.2011 was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer determining market value of the lands acquired at a sum of Rs.74,000/- per acre.
The landloosers sought reference under Section 18(1) of the Act which was registered as LAC Nos.86/2012, 82/2012 and 80/2012.
The reference court recorded the evidence of one of the claimants in LAC No.82/2012 and marked Exs.P1 to P32.

The respondents marked copy of the award by consent as Ex.R1.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the reference Court enhanced the compensation from Rs.74,000/- to a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- along with all statutory benefits, costs and interest.
6. Being aggrieved by the award passed by the reference Court, the landloosers have filed these appeals.

The learned counsel for the appellants/landloosers contend that the lands in Hegadihal village lying within Bijapur Taluk and the lands in Ukkalli village, Basavanabagewadi Taluk of Bijapur were acquired for the purpose of construction of Minor Irrigation Tank.
He submits that these two villages lie adjacent to each other and soil type of both these lands were similar and both these lands were provided with some irrigation facility.

Therefore, the market value of the land in Ukkalli village Sri.Bhimappa And Ors vs The Assistant Commissioner And Ors on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156729214/
5 determined at Rs.10,95,246/- per acre ought to have been awarded in respect of the lands in Hegadihal village.

entities.text: Sri.Bhimappa And Ors vs The Assistant Commissioner And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellants relied upon the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.200542/2016 and connected appeals where this court was considering an appeal arising out of the reference proceedings in respect of the lands in Ukkalli village and this Court confirmed the compensation payable at a sum of Rs.10,95,246/- per acre.

The learned counsel therefore, submitted that since both the villages lie adjacent to each other and both the lands were comparable and were acquired for the same project, the compensation as determined in respect of Ukkalli village must have been awarded in respect of the land lying in Hegadihal village.

Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader submits that the appellants/landloosers had restricted their appeals to a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- and therefore, this Court cannot enhance the compensation beyond a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- claimed by the appellants.

In this regard, he relied upon the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.200799/2014 and connected appeals, in respect of Hegadihal village, where landloosers had restricted their claim for enhancement to an extent of Rs.1,00,000/- over and above what was ordered by the reference Court.
This Court had enhanced the compensation payable by a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
He submits that even when a review petition was filed, the Division Bench refused to review its judgment.
He therefore, submits that once the landloosers restricted their claim for enhancement, they are not entitled for higher compensation.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondents.
10. The fact that the lands in Hegadihal village and Ukkalli village were acquired for the purpose of Minor Irrigation NC: 2023:KHC-K:5597 Project is not in dispute.
This only makes it more than apparent that both these lands lie adjacent to each other and were acquired for the same purpose.

A mere location of the lands in two different talukas does not change the market value of the property and the Division Bench of this Court having once held that the market value of land in Ukkalli village was a sum of Rs.10,95,246/- per acre, there is no escape for the State to contend that the compensation payable in respect of Hegadihal village could anything be less than a sum of Rs.10,95,246/- per acre.

It is now trite law that the Courts are not restricted to enhance the compensation to the amount claimed by the claimants having regard to the nature and scope of Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act and for the purpose of grant of just compensation as envisaged under Article 31(c) of the Constitution of India.
11. In that view of the matter, these appeals are allowed.
The compensation awarded by the reference Court is enhanced from Rs.5,00,000/- per acre to a sum of Rs.10,95,246/- per acre along with all interests, costs, solatium and benefits.
